cands.name: Oliver G. Gilbert III
cands.bio: Democratic nominee in FL-24 (open seat; Rep. Frederica Wilson not running). Attorney; Miami Gardens council member (2008) and mayor (2012-2020); Miami-Dade County commissioner for District 1 from Nov 2020 until he left to run in June 2026; chaired the commission in 2023. Won 7-way primary with about 34%.
cands.local_ties: Born in Miami Gardens, Aug 15, 1972; FAMU and University of Miami law graduate (Wikipedia).

record.text: Mayor of Miami Gardens 2012-2020 and Miami-Dade County commissioner (District 1) since Nov 17, 2020; elected commission chair unanimously in Dec 2022.

Campaign priorities reported by WLRN: affordability through stronger unions and worker protections, Congress reclaiming control of tariffs, social services with job creation, healthcare as a right pursued incrementally.

money_notes.text: Crypto-backed super PAC Fairshake, through affiliate Protect Progress, spent more than $2 million trying to defeat him in the Aug 2026 Democratic primary; he won anyway. The article does not list Fairshake's donors.

controversies.text: Local press criticized him for attacking primary rival Shevrin Jones over Jones's vote to rename Palm Beach International Airport after Donald Trump, though Gilbert had himself voted for the 2024 Palm Avenue street co-naming (see votes).

In Aug 2026 mass texts falsely claiming Jones was HIV-positive were sent under the name of Equality Florida; an Equality Florida spokesperson criticized Gilbert and other candidates for not denouncing the tactic. Gilbert called the claim 'a lie' and said it 'needs to stop.'

endorsements.text: Rep. Frederica Wilson (retiring incumbent), Miami-Dade Mayor Daniella Levine Cava, Miami Mayor Eileen Higgins; AFSCME, AFL-CIO and UNITE HERE named as union allies.

cands.gaps: Only 2 of the 6 requested commission roll-call votes could be verified from opened sources (commission minutes/Legistar were not retrievable in time). Miami Gardens mayor/council votes not retrieved. Campaign site/social links not verified. No AIPAC or other outside spending found in the sources opened.

votes.bill: Resolution co-designating Palm Avenue in Hialeah as 'President Donald J. Trump Avenue' (Dec 2024)
votes.what: Approved a ceremonial street co-naming for a city-maintained road; passed as part of the consent agenda.

votes.bill: Override of Mayor Levine Cava's veto of the South Dade Logistics and Technology District (Nov 2022)
votes.what: Overrode the mayor's veto, allowing a 378-acre industrial project outside the county's Urban Development Boundary to move ahead; override needs two-thirds of the commission.
